This study introduces a new implicit-explicit Runge-Kutta framework designed for solving hyperbolic systems with source terms, where the sources introduce strong nonlinearities. The proposed scheme employs a splitting technique that isolates the treatment of source terms from the hyperbolic component, applying a fully implicit Runge-Kutta method to the latter and the fully explicit version to the former. A primary challenge in this approach lies in managing the hyperbolic boundary conditions during the implicit stages. To address this, we develop a novel boundary treatment strategy that resolves the issue effectively. Furthermore, we establish the convergence of the resulting time-stepping scheme. Finally, numerical experiments are conducted to validate the method's performance and demonstrate its efficiency.

We introduce a new 3D back reflector utilizing silicon photonic crystals, designed to enhance absorption in thin and ultra-thin silicon layers. This structure is built by patterning silicon nanowires into a hexagonal lattice and integrating them with a silicon dioxide spacer layer. The photonic crystal's bandgap is tuned to the target wavelength by adjusting the nanowire pitch and diameter. Theoretical analysis indicates that this design achieves a 100% absorption rate in a 100 nm silicon film at 1550 nm, with an absorption coefficient of 99% for a 1000 nm silicon layer. The device's performance is further optimized by incorporating a top anti-reflection coating.

Uncertainty is a fundamental aspect of the world, and reasoning effectively under such conditions is vital for intelligent systems. While current artificial systems excel at logical deduction, they often struggle to model the inherent uncertainty found in real-world scenarios. To address this, we introduce the Credal Valuation Network (CrVN), a graphical model designed to represent uncertain beliefs. We demonstrate that CrVN can be constructed from natural language using the Credal Logic framework, which extends traditional logic to handle uncertainty. Furthermore, we outline a method for reasoning within CrVN by leveraging its connection to Valuation Networks (VNs), a class of graphical models. Experimental results indicate that the Credal Valuation Network is both effective and efficient for performing uncertain reasoning.

Top-K recommendation has become a standard approach in recommender systems. Although neural network-based methods have achieved significant success, they often fail to account for the inherent uncertainty in user preferences and item representations. To address this gap, we introduce a new probabilistic metric learning framework designed to enhance top-K recommendation. Our approach utilizes a margin loss to pull positive user-item pairs closer together while pushing negative examples apart. Additionally, we incorporate an adaptive margin mechanism to dynamically adjust the margin size for each training sample, thereby improving the model's generalization capability. Extensive experiments conducted on two real-world datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

The concept of non-Markovianity in quantum channels is defined by the non-monotonic behavior of trace-distance metrics between quantum states. This behavior is linked to the reversibility of the channel, as demonstrated by the fact that trace-distance monotonicity implies the process is completely positive and therefore non-Markovian. Conversely, it is established that the presence of non-Markovianity in trace-distance signifies reversibility. This work demonstrates that non-unitary channels, specifically those that are not completely positive, can exhibit non-monotonic behavior in trace-distance indefinitely, even when the process is completely non-reversible. This finding is significant because it indicates that non-Markovianity in trace-distance serves as a robust indicator of the eternal reversibility of non-unitary channels, thereby establishing a novel criterion for assessing non-Markovianity in quantum channels.

This study introduces a novel framework for active learning and effective classification that integrates counterfactual reasoning. By employing a counterfactual reasoning model to analyze instances, the system generates hypothetical scenarios to pinpoint the most critical features for classification. These identified features are then used to guide the selection of the most informative unlabeled data points. Experiments conducted on both real-world and synthetic datasets demonstrate that this approach achieves superior classification accuracy compared to existing methods while utilizing fewer labeled samples.

Robotic Simulated Surroundings for Evaluation and Benchmarking of Semantic Mapping Algorithms (RoSmEEry) is a simulator designed to assess and benchmark semantic mapping techniques. It offers a comprehensive suite of tools, including a 3D visualizer, a physics engine, and a data logging system, enabling the testing of algorithms within realistic, complex environments. The platform supports the testing of various sensor configurations, such as RGB-D cameras, LIDAR, and sonar, and allows users to define custom sensor models. Additionally, it features a data logging interface to record sensor inputs and robot trajectories. The primary objective of RoSmEEry is to facilitate the rigorous evaluation and comparison of semantic mapping methods across diverse scenarios.

Rikudo is a two-player turn-based strategy game in which players alternate placing tiles on a grid. Each tile features a number from 1 to 4, and during placement, a player must select a direction to extend the path by that many spaces. The objective is to create the longest continuous path in any direction. This game, originally released in 2019, has been mathematically proven to be NP-hard. The following provides a self-contained proof of this result.

Optimal Transport (OT) is a mathematical framework for quantifying the disparity between two probability distributions. While OT has gained significant traction in machine learning, its computational demands often hinder its application to large-scale problems. This article provides a comprehensive survey of numerical methodologies for OT, with a particular focus on strategies that mitigate computational costs. We examine both the theoretical foundations and the practical implementation of these techniques, alongside their applications in machine learning. Furthermore, we discuss the challenges inherent in OT problems and outline promising future research directions.

Ramanujan proposed three identities concerning modular equations of degree 5, 3, and 7. In this paper, we present novel proofs for these identities alongside generalizations involving the Hecke groups.

We present new redshift measurements for the host galaxies of eight lensed quasars, utilizing high-resolution spectra obtained from the Keck Observatory. These observations were conducted as part of the TDCOSMO initiative, which aims to refine the Hubble constant ($H_0$) by measuring time delays in gravitationally lensed quasars. By analyzing the lensing galaxies, we derived their redshifts and calculated the velocity dispersion of the stellar populations within the host systems. Our results indicate that the new host redshifts align well with those previously established in the literature, with the exception of the host galaxy in the system Q0957+561. For this specific case, we determined a redshift of $z=0.3701 \pm 0.0003$, which is notably lower than the value of $z=0.3729 \pm 0.0003$ reported in the H0LiCOW analysis. This discrepancy is likely attributable to the fact that the H0LiCOW study relied on a single absorption line, whereas our analysis incorporated a broader range of spectral features. Furthermore, we measured the velocity dispersions of the lensing galaxies, finding that the new values are consistent with those derived from the literature.

This study introduces a novel approach for addressing nonlinear $q$-fractional differential equations defined on time scales by leveraging the inverse $q$-Hadamard fractional integral. The method employs $q$-exponential polynomials as fundamental solutions to the homogeneous homogeneous $q$-homogeneous $q$-fractional differential equation. Furthermore, the paper establishes the existence and uniqueness of solutions for $q$-fractional boundary value problems utilizing the Banach fixed point theorem and the nonlinear alternative of Lazer, Levine, and Lazer. The proposed methodology is illustrated through specific examples.

The phonon Hall effect (PHE) in magnetically ordered crystals is a prominent example of a topological phenomenon. This study demonstrates that the Hall conductivity associated with phonons in such systems is quantized, with the value determined by the Chern number of phonon bands. We establish that this topological constraint holds even when magnetic anisotropy is present. Furthermore, we show that the presence of magnetic anisotropy can be utilized to manipulate the sign of the Hall conductivity, offering a practical method for controlling the PHE.

Nod-and-shuffle (N&S) spectral imaging is a method that acquires a complete spectral dataset by sequentially capturing images at different spectral positions. This approach is particularly advantageous for hyperspectral imaging because it is compatible with standard, cost-effective cameras and avoids the need for expensive spectral scanning mechanisms. This study introduces a novel implementation of N&S spectral imaging tailored for broad-field excitation using Shifted Excitation Raman Difference Spectroscopy (SERDS). The proposed system utilizes a single excitation wavelength to illuminate the entire field of view, with the telescope's focal plane shifted laterally to access distinct regions. The resulting spectra are processed to eliminate Raman signals from the background, leaving only the signal originating from the target area. This methodology was validated through experiments involving a plastic sample, demonstrating the system's capability to generate hyperspectral images of the target region.

This study establishes matrix Fejér and Levin-Stejn inequalities within the framework of Fejér and Levin-Stejn kernels. The Fejér kernel is defined as the sum of powers of a unitary matrix, while the Levin-Stejn kernel is defined as the sum of powers of a self-adjoint matrix multiplied by specific coefficients. By leveraging these definitions, we derive matrix extensions of the Fejér and Levin-Stejn inequalities. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Fejér kernel corresponds to the chromatic polynomial of a Cayley graph, and the Levin-Stejn kernel corresponds to the weighted chromatic polynomial of a directed graph.

We investigate the mean null energy condition (CNEC) within the context of an evaporating black hole in the bulk, utilizing a holographic framework. Our findings indicate that the CNE is violated in the vicinity of the black hole's horizon, yet it holds true for the entire exterior region.

We examine the scaling dimensions of operators within conformal field theory, emphasizing the double-scaling limit where the massless limit and the large-N limit are taken simultaneously. This approach yields a solvable model for analyzing the spectrum of scaling dimensions, demonstrating that the primary field content is governed by the Airy function. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the leading scaling dimension scales as N², supporting the conjecture that this behavior persists in the string theory dual description.

Industrial Control Systems (ICS) are increasingly integrated into critical infrastructure, such as manufacturing, transportation, and energy sectors, necessitating robust cybersecurity measures. To address this, the authors introduce a maturity model designed to assess and enhance the cybersecurity posture of ICS environments. This model offers a structured framework for organizations to identify vulnerabilities, prioritize remediation efforts, and continuously elevate their security defenses.

Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is a critical area of research with significant potential for real-world applications. However, the inherent complexity of MARL, which involves multiple agents, often hinders the development of effective learning algorithms. To address this, we introduce a new MARL framework called the Greedy-based Worth Representation (GWR) designed to enhance coordination among agents. By employing a greedy approach, GWR identifies the most valuable actions for each agent, thereby reducing the action space and accelerating the learning process. We demonstrate that the proposed algorithm is provably optimal and empirically validate its effectiveness through experiments on the classic StarCraft II game.

Pretrained language models (PLMs) are widely used across numerous fields, including natural language understanding, machine translation, and text generation. However, these models are trained on vast datasets that often contain human biases, raising concerns about whether such biases are inadvertently encoded into the models. This paper introduces StereoSet, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the extent to which PLMs exhibit gender stereotypes. We demonstrate that this benchmark effectively quantifies such biases and offer a comprehensive analysis of how various PLMs perform on these stereotypical associations.

Optimizing the tilt angle of solar panels is critical for maximizing energy output. While existing literature predominantly focuses on online policies, this paper introduces an off-policy learning approach to tilt optimization that leverages historical data. By utilizing the Fitted Q-iteration (FQI) algorithm, we develop a policy capable of generating tilt angle sequences that outperform standard single-angle settings. Our method's efficacy is validated through simulations on a photovoltaic system, demonstrating its practical applicability.

This study examines the CKM angle $\gamma$ by integrating two independent measurements from the LHCb experiment: the ratio $|A_{\bar{B}^0_{\rm d} \to K^+ K^-} / A_{B^0_{\rm d} \to K^+ K^-}|$ and the angle $\phi_{\rm scs}$. The analysis yields a value of $\gamma = (0.21 \pm 0.10) \times \pi$ radians. Furthermore, we present a new determination of $\gamma$ derived from the combination of all available LHCb results. The resulting value is $\gamma = (0.21 \pm 0.05) \times \pi$ radians.
This paper examines the conditions under which a real ellipsoid defined by $\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2 + \sum_{i,j=1}^n a_{ij}x_i\bar{x}_j = 1$ within $\mathbb{C}^n$ possesses symmetry about its center.

In the contemporary digital landscape, individuals frequently exchange personal data with corporations in exchange for goods and services. This paper investigates how well individuals comprehend the risks and benefits associated with such data markets. We conducted a survey of 1,000 participants to gauge their willingness to share information and their perceptions of privacy risks, followed by a controlled experiment where subjects were informed of specific risks and benefits before expressing their willingness to share. Our findings reveal that people tend to overestimate the benefits of data sharing while simultaneously holding a pessimistic view of the associated risks. Furthermore, the perceived value of sharing appears to vary based on the survey respondent's demographic and psychographic characteristics.

This paper introduces a deep learning-driven approach to list sphere decoding for Faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling, specifically targeting the detection of transmitted symbols. The proposed method employs a neural network to forecast the likelihood of each candidate symbol being the true transmission, thereby guiding the expansion of the search list within the sphere decoding framework. Experimental findings indicate that this deep learning-enhanced list sphere decoding surpasses conventional sphere decoding methods in terms of performance.

This work examines the Frink ideal structure within effect algebras, establishing both the order-theoretic and order-independent characterizations of these ideals. It is demonstrated that every Frink ideal in an effect algebra corresponds to a specific open set, a correspondence that defines a Frink ideal's associated open set and its closure. Furthermore, the study explores the topological properties of these associated open sets, examines the topological nature of effect algebras, and investigates the relationship between the topology and Frink ideal structure.

Data augmentation is a fundamental technique for enhancing the generalization capabilities of deep learning models. While numerous methods have been developed to generate novel synthetic data, most rely on random transformations that often lack semantic coherence. To address this, we introduce SaliencyMix, a saliency-guided augmentation strategy that synthesizes new samples by blending regions of interest from distinct images. By leveraging saliency maps to identify key semantic components, our method ensures that the resulting augmented data maintains semantic integrity. Empirical evaluations across various tasks and datasets demonstrate that SaliencyMix effectively regularizes models and yields superior performance compared to conventional augmentation approaches.

We demonstrate that any partial trace defined on an infinite Iwahori-Hecke algebra associated with a finite type must be a linear combination of existing fully defined partial traces. Furthermore, we examine the space of partial traces, detailing a specific basis and providing formulas for both the left and right multiplication operators. We also establish that the Hecke action on this space is finite, and we determine the spectrum of these left and right multiplication operators.

Intrinsic galaxy alignments (IGA) represent a significant source of systematic error in weak lensing studies. While previous research has primarily focused on the impact of IGA on the two-point galaxy-galaxy lensing signal, we investigate its influence on the two-point cosmic shear correlation function. Our analysis utilizes the EFTofIA framework to model IGA effects within the context of the $\Lambda$CDM cosmology. We further examine how these effects vary under modified gravity scenarios, specifically within the Horndeski class of theories. Our findings indicate that the IGA-induced bias in the cosmic shear power spectrum is approximately 10% of the magnitude observed in the galaxy-galaxy lens signal. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the IGA signal in the cosmic shear spectrum is highly sensitive to the parameters governing modified gravity. Consequently, we argue that incorporating the IGA signal into future weak lensing analyses will enhance the precision of constraints on new physics.

This study investigates the rheological behavior of systems composed of deformable spheres, specifically focusing on the interplay between particle shape and the resulting rheology. We examine two distinct types of deformation: elongation into ellipsoids and flattening into oblate spheroids. Our findings indicate that the rheological response is governed by the specific nature of the shape change. In the case of oblate spheroids, the system exhibits a shear-thinning flow curve, a characteristic typically associated with rigid particles. Conversely, elongated particles display a shear-thinning normal stress difference, a trait usually observed in rigid, deformable systems. These results demonstrate that particle deformation fundamentally alters the mechanisms driving rheological behavior, thereby blurring the traditional distinctions between the rheology of rigid and deformable particles.

This study introduces a data-driven approach to model the melting of gold nanoparticles, utilizing a coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulation framework. The system's behavior is governed by a two-state kinetic model that accounts for the coexistence of crystalline and liquid phases. The transition rates between phases are formulated as a function of the particle's temperature and size, with parameters derived through a Bayesian inference method. This statistical technique leverages extensive experimental data regarding melting points across various sizes to constrain the model. The resulting kinetic framework successfully reproduces melting point trends observed in prior studies and generates novel predictions for melting points at sizes where experimental data is absent.

This research investigates the existence of bifurcations and branching phenomena within parameter-dependent nonlinear equations. We establish a general theorem that links the splitting of potential operators to these problems, thereby extending numerous established bifurcations and splitting theorems found in existing literature.

This study establishes weight-beta parametric identities for weighted p-adic (h,q)-Genochi numbers and polynomials.

This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning (RL) approach for estimating long-term treatment effects. The method utilizes a specialized RL framework to derive an optimal policy that minimizes the discrepancy between the estimated outcome and the true outcome of interest. We demonstrate that this RL-based estimator achieves a convergence rate of $\mathcal{O}(N^{-1/2})$, where $N$ represents the sample size. Additionally, the method is adaptable to scenarios involving sequential treatments.

Case-control studies are frequently utilized to investigate risk factor–disease associations, yet they are susceptible to selection bias, particularly when controls are not drawn from the same population as cases. This bias is often mitigated through matching, which can inadvertently introduce further biases, such as recall bias. This occurs when cases remember and report risk factor data more accurately than controls. This study introduces a method to address recall bias within the framework of causal inference. By employing inverse probability weighting, we aim to eliminate the bias caused by differential recall rates between cases and controls. We demonstrate that this weighting strategy enables the estimation of the causal effect of risk factors on disease risk, even in the presence of differential recall. Additionally, we propose a method to evaluate the impact of unobserved confounding on the estimated effects derived from weighted analyses.

Generative models have recently achieved remarkable success across various domains, including image and audio synthesis, as well as natural language processing. While generative autoencoders (GAEs) offer a particularly efficient and straightforward approach to modeling complex data distributions, they are typically trained using maximum likelihood estimation via the reparameterization trick. This method relies on approximating the gradient of the log-likelihood, which results in a computationally expensive procedure that is often infeasible for high-dimensional datasets. To address this limitation, we introduce a new training framework for GAEs that enables exact maximum likelihood optimization without approximation. Our approach utilizes a specialized layer architecture that allows for the efficient calculation of the true gradient. We validate this method on image datasets such as MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10, demonstrating that our exact training strategy significantly outperforms standard approximate techniques.

Urban data is characterized by its vast volume, high dimensionality, and intricate interconnections. To effectively analyze such data, it is essential to identify patterns that reveal relationships among attributes, thereby enabling the discovery of valuable insights. This paper introduces a new approach for visualizing and analyzing correlations between attributes within city datasets. The method operates in two phases: initially, it extracts correlated attribute patterns from the dataset, and subsequently, it presents these patterns through a novel visualization tool. The core of this visualization is a graph where nodes represent attributes and edges signify their inter-correlations. The system supports interactive exploration, allowing users to query specific attributes and dynamically adjust graph layouts to facilitate pattern discovery. We have implemented this approach in a web-based application and evaluated its effectiveness using two real-world city datasets. The results demonstrate that the proposed method is both practical and effective for uncovering correlated patterns in urban data.

This study introduces a geometric multigrid preconditioner tailored for the discrete systems resulting from the application of the hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) method with polynomial degree zero (HDG-P0) to reaction-diffusion equations and the generalized Stokes equations. The preconditioner employs a semi-coarse space defined by a coarse grid combined with local correction mechanisms. A key finding is that the preconditioned operator exhibits a uniformly bounded condition number relative to the fine grid's polynomial degree and mesh resolution. This result is proven through a novel application of the Babuška--Schauder argument, which establishes a lower bound for the coercivity of the preconditioned operator. Furthermore, numerical experiments confirm the preconditioner's efficiency and robustness.

The $e$-value serves as a metric for quantifying the magnitude of bias in missing data scenarios. This study introduces a Bayesian approach to sensitivity analysis, utilizing the $e$-value to identify upper bounds for bias within the imputed region. We further demonstrate that this methodology yields a posterior distribution for the imputation bias, thereby establishing a Bayesian framework for sensitivity analysis.

Multivariate crossover trials are frequently employed in clinical research to evaluate the efficacy and safety of pharmaceutical interventions. Nevertheless, attrition remains a significant challenge, particularly in lengthy studies, which can compromise the validity of findings. This paper introduces a novel probability-driven framework for managing missing data within these trials. The methodology utilizes a multiple imputation strategy that incorporates both the efficacy and safety metrics of participants. By modeling the probability distribution of outcomes based on the crossover design, we generate missing data estimates that reflect the specific trial structure. We demonstrate that this approach yields valid parameter estimates and valid statistical inferences, even in the presence of missing data. The proposed method is validated using a simulation study and further illustrated with data from a clinical trial assessing the effects of a specific medication.

We present a weak monoidal structure applicable to any category, utilizing the Stasheff polytope (also known as the Stasheff associahedron) to define the product and identity components. This framework accommodates a broad spectrum of structures, encompassing standard monoidal categories as well as various higher categories.

DRAM is the primary memory component in modern computing systems, yet its performance and energy efficiency are constrained by the serial nature of its access protocol. To address this, recent research has explored custom DRAM protocols that enable in-memory parallelism and optimized data movement. However, widespread adoption of these advanced DRAMs is currently hindered by prohibitively high costs. To overcome this barrier, we introduce CODIC, a low-cost substrate designed to facilitate custom DRAM protocols. CODIC consists of a programmable logic controller and a set of DRAM-specific functional units, including a DRAM controller, a DRAM data mover, and a DRAM register file. The data mover and register file are constructed using DRAM I/O pins and internal storage, respectively, ensuring minimal fabrication overhead. This article series explores the application of functional programming to coordinate and manage network resources. The initial installment examined the specific technical attributes of functional languages that render them suitable for this purpose, while the current paper addresses the broader challenges of managing and coordinating network resources. It outlines the essential principles for managing and evolving software-defined networks, emphasizing that a clear evolution strategy is critical for success. The series concludes in Part III, which will focus on practical implementation aspects, including the necessary tools and methodologies for deploying these concepts.

The toric code serves as a foundational model for topological quantum error correction, a field essential for achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation. This research investigates the resource requirements for executing two-qubit gates on toric code states, specifically comparing the overhead of implementing these operations using the surface code versus a theoretical framework involving infinite qubits. We demonstrate that while certain two-qubit gates can be realized with a constant count of operations across both models, other gates require a constant count for the surface code but scale linearly with the total number of qubits in the idealized infinite model. Furthermore, we extend this analysis to multi-qubit gates, proving that any such operation demands gate counts that grow at least linearly with the number of qubits involved, regardless of whether the architecture is based on a surface code or an infinite lattice.

The Virtual Observatory (VO) was established to standardize interoperability across diverse astronomical data sources, encompassing observatories, surveys, and archives. While the VO's primary focus has historically been data, the VO Observables (VOOP) and other frameworks aim to extend these principles to observational tasks and observing facilities. This paper introduces OPUS, a task control system designed to manage requests for both the Virtual Observatory and the Physical Observatory. OPUS operates by defining a comprehensive set of observables that cover the entire observing lifecycle, from initial planning and scheduling to execution and data retrieval. These observables are organized into task types, each linked to specific VO standards for input and output. OPUS is built upon the X-TASKS specification, which defines a common XML interface for task control systems. This interface is being developed into an open standard to ensure widespread adoption. The paper details the OPUS architecture, its current capabilities, and outlines the roadmap for future development.

The paper introduces a digital game designed to enhance the teaching of wireless networking concepts, specifically 802.11 Wi-Fi. It details the development of this digital game alongside its integration into an educational setting. The authors also examine how this digital game-driven approach impacts student performance and the value of digital game-driven learning. The findings indicate that students utilizing digital game-driven learning achieved higher scores on a post-game test compared to those in a traditional lecture group, with the former also demonstrating a greater ability to apply their knowledge.

Ozone (O3) serves as a primary proxy for detecting molecular oxygen (O2) in exoplanet atmospheres, given that O2 is difficult to observe directly. This study examines the O2-O3 relationship in Earth-like worlds, focusing on the link between their abundances and the impact of competing photochemical and hydrological processes. We demonstrate that O3 levels are governed by the balance between O2 photolysis and the destruction of HOx radicals, which are generated by O3 photolysis. Consequently, the O2/O3 ratio is not fixed but depends on the atmospheric water vapor content. We further show that the O3 abundance is highly sensitive to the rate of water vapor replenishment, a factor that is difficult to constrain for exoplanets. These findings indicate that O3 cannot reliably indicate O2 levels in all Earth-like exoplanets, particularly those with low water vapor.

We investigate the 3D Hofstadter model, which features a constant magnetic field applied along the $z$-axis. Our findings indicate that, in the thermodynamic limit, the system sustains a robust, quantized, and dissipationless current flowing along the $z$-direction, provided the system is driven by a specific type of electric field. This current is a bulk phenomenon, distinguished from edge or surface currents, and persists even in the absence of a magnetic field.

This study explores the application of Neural Machine Translation (NMT) for Medical Neural Interpretation (MNI) using a multilingual framework. The research evaluates the performance of domain-adapted versus non-adapted MNI models across English, French, and Spanish, employing the MedNLI corpus for assessment. The outcomes demonstrate that domain adaptation significantly enhances performance across all evaluated languages.

This study introduces a new sentence representation pretraining approach designed to enhance the performance of compact cross-lingual and monolingual retrieval systems. Unlike prior methods that rely on sentence embeddings derived solely from local word-level information, our technique incorporates context-awareness by integrating surrounding sentences. Specifically, we develop a new unsupervised pretraining objective that leverages this contextual information to improve the quality of sentence representations. We also present a Context-Aware Contrastive Learning (CAL) framework to optimize these representations. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in both monolingual and cross-lingual retrieval tasks, particularly when used with lightweight neural architectures.

Multimodal learning has gained significant traction in recent years, yet most existing methods rely on simple averaging to combine features from various modalities, thereby overlooking the inherent heterogeneity among them. To address this limitation, we introduce Prototypical Modal Adjustment (PMR), a new framework designed to capture modality-specific characteristics. PMR operates in three phases: first, it constructs modality-specific prototypes; second, it aligns modalities by measuring the discrepancy between each modality and its corresponding prototype; and third, it recalibrates modal representations based on this alignment. By integrating these adjusted representations, the model produces a final output. Empirical results demonstrate that PMR outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques across various tasks, including image-text matching, visual question answering, and open-domain question answering.

This study examines the impact of vector engagement on the equilibrium state and transport theory within the Vlasov-Poisson framework. Specifically, we demonstrate that the equilibrium Vlasov function is no longer monotonically increasing with respect to the kinetic energy of the equilibrium. Furthermore, the proof of the adiabatic theorem for the transport equation relies on the novel concept of the "splitting entropy," which is defined as a specific entropy that decreases monotonically over time.

This study introduces a novel spoken command recognition architecture that integrates Tensor-Train (TT) networks with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) units. The proposed CNN-LSTM-TT framework leverages the capabilities of both hybrid TT models and CNNs to enhance performance. Specifically, the TT component is designed to capture long-range temporal dependencies, while the CNNs extract features from the input data. The model is trained using a dataset of 10 distinct commands, each containing 100 samples. The results demonstrate that the hybrid approach outperforms standalone TT models, achieving a 100% accuracy rate on the test set.

We demonstrate that a single open quantum system can be described by multiple equivalent yet distinct master equation formulations, which correspond to various different quantum-jump paths. This work establishes a master equation formulation for a specific class of non-Markovian processes, where the dynamics are defined by a sequence of random non-unitary maps. We show that, for any such non-Markovian model, it is feasible to construct a sequence of Markovian models that replicate its temporal evolution.

This study investigates the optical absorption enhancement in amorphous silicon (a-Si) thin-film solar cells by integrating plasmonic nanoparticles (PNPs) at the rear interface. The analysis evaluates the influence of nanoparticle shape, size, and concentration on absorption enhancement and device efficiency. Results indicate that spherical PNPs with a radius of 50 nm provide the superior performance, boosting the short-circuit current density ($J_{sc}$) by 10.1% and the power conversion efficiency (PCE) by 1.1% compared to control cells. The research further examines the impact of varying particle sizes and concentrations, revealing that larger particles and higher concentrations yield greater enhancements. Additionally, the study explores the role of particle shape, demonstrating that while spherical particles offer the best results, platelet-shaped particles with a thickness of 10 nm and a radius of 50 nm provide a comparable improvement of 1.0% in PCE. The findings confirm that plasmonic nanoparticles serve as an effective strategy for optimizing the performance of thin-film solar cells.

This paper investigates the expressive capabilities of a first-order logic (FOL) framework that lacks the enumeration construct but incorporates a choice operator. We demonstrate that this system is strictly less expressive than standard First-Order Logic (FOL) and can be embedded within Datalog with fixpoint. Furthermore, we establish that, under the assumption that P ≠ NP, any formula in this system can be translated into a Datalog program with fixpoint that runs in polynomial time.

This paper introduces a hardware- and algorithm-aware co-design framework for LSTM networks, specifically targeting video recognition tasks. The methodology involves three key components: first, applying Hierarchical Tucker (HTK) tensor decomposition to the LSTM's weight tensors; second, utilizing a novel algorithm to optimize the HTK order and the network's depth and width; and third, implementing a hardware-aware pruning strategy to lower memory usage and computational demands. Experimental results indicate that the proposed co-design approach achieves superior accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art models while maintaining a comparable level of sparsity.

The MAVLink protocol serves as the primary communication standard for unmanned systems, including drones and airships, facilitating interaction between vehicles and their ground control stations. Despite its widespread adoption, the protocol lacks built-in security measures, leaving it vulnerable to various attacks. This paper introduces MAVSec, a lightweight security framework designed to secure communications for ArduPilot and PX*P platforms. MAVSec integrates seamlessly with existing system operations, requiring no modifications to the underlying MAVLink implementation. The authors detail the specific security threats facing the protocol and demonstrate how MAVSec mitigates these risks. Additionally, the study evaluates the framework's performance through comprehensive benchmarking and a real-world security assessment involving physical attacks on a UAV.

We introduce Kollaps, a distributed, high-performance system designed for emulating network topologies. Kollaps offers two key capabilities: first, it supports the creation of dynamic topologies by allowing the addition or removal of nodes and links at any moment; second, it enables the simultaneous execution of identical experiments across numerous emulated topologies. To achieve this, Kollaps employs a distributed architecture that ensures both high performance and scalability. We evaluated Kollaps by running 100,000 emulated instances of the Twitter follower network, each containing 100 nodes and 1,000 edges. Our results demonstrate that Kollaps can emulate these configurations at a rate of 10,000 executions per second. Furthermore, we compared Kollaps with two existing systems, Dask and Ray, for executing experiments on dynamic topologies.

This paper presents a new class of exact solutions to the Einstein-Maxwell equations, which can be generated from any arbitrary solution of the Einstein equations. These solutions are formulated within a four-dimensional conformal framework using a specific coordinate system defined by three complex twistor coordinates and one real null coordinate. The metric for such a solution comprises an initial metric multiplied by a scaling factor, with the scaling factor determined by the underlying original solution. A defining feature of this family is the presence of a null vector field that undergoes complexification. The discussion also explores the implications of these complex null vectors for the Newman-Penrose formalism and the structure of twistor space.

The muon detector developed for the study is designed to operate within the Gran Sasso National Laboratory, situated beneath 4000 meters of rock overburden. This device is engineered to capture and analyze the rare flux of cosmic-ray muons that penetrate the underground facility. The system comprises a 1x1 meter active area, consisting of a 1 mm thick scintillator sheet segmented into 16 strips, coupled with 16 photomultiplier tubes. The scintillator strips are read out using 16 Avalanche Photodiodes (APDs) to facilitate high-speed data acquisition. The detector's primary objective is to map the three-dimensional distribution of density within the laboratory by correlating the time-of-flight and energy loss of individual muons with their specific trajectories.

Parsing Expressions constitute a concise, high-level language designed to describe context-free grammars for parsing. While numerous online parsers exist to process such expressions, they typically lack support for the full syntax, such as the ability to assign names to subexpressions. This paper introduces a novel extension to Parsing Expressions that allows for named subexpressions, presents a corresponding formal grammar, and demonstrates an implementation using LLVM's C++ library parser generator.

We investigate the vacuum Cherenkov effect in a thermal bath, specifically examining how finite-temperature modifications to the photon dispersion relation influence the phenomenon. Our findings indicate that the maximum Cherenkov velocity for a thermal photon is invariably lower than that of a zero-temperature photon. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this maximum Cherenkov velocity for photons in a thermal environment increases as the temperature decreases.

We introduce a method for monitoring the evolution of language by leveraging the inherent unpredictability of neural language models. This approach utilizes the temporal dynamics of prediction loss to identify shifts in linguistic style and content. Our findings indicate that these shifts are accurately detected by measuring prediction loss across varying time windows, a process that requires no manual feature engineering. Furthermore, the model's sensitivity to context length allows it to pinpoint specific events, such as the election of Barack Obama, by analyzing text from just a few weeks prior to the occurrence.

We introduce a novel approach to 3D object pose estimation that leverages the visual changes caused by rotating an object. By utilizing a dataset of objects that have been rotated in place, we can train a neural network to predict a 3D orientation from a single image and the object's current rotation state. This method is particularly advantageous for robotic systems equipped with turntables, which can be used to rotate an object to capture a novel viewpoint. Our results demonstrate that the proposed network achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art pose estimators that rely on multiple images. Furthermore, we show that our approach can be combined with existing single-view methods to further enhance accuracy.

This study examines charge transport in a hybrid superconductor-semiconductor system featuring a semiconductor nanowire with strong spin-orbit coupling, subjected to a magnetic field parallel to its axis and subjected to a crossed electric field. We identify two distinct tunneling regimes: crossed Andreev tunneling (CAT) and elastic co-reflection (CER). The presence of topological Andreev bound states (ABSs) in the superconductor enables the control of both CAT and CER through the manipulation of the semiconductor's electrostatic potential. Notably, the coexistence of ABSs and CER allows for the independent regulation of these two processes via the perpendicular and parallel components of the applied electric field.

This study examines particle acceleration during magnetic reconnection within a two-dimensional, collisionless plasma featuring a Harris sheet configuration. We introduce a novel approach that incorporates ad hoc angle-scattering to simulate the impact of Coulomb collisions on particle dynamics. Our findings indicate that particle heating occurs primarily through a first-order Fermi mechanism, driven by the systematic reflection of particles off reconnection-generated Alfvénic fluctuations. Furthermore, we observe that the inclusion of collisional scattering suppresses the net particle energy gain.

This study examines a simplified extended Higgs sector featuring a real singlet scalar, where the scalar potential is defined by a single free parameter. We investigate the sensitivity of the Higgs boson's couplings to other parameters within this framework using combined data from $e^+e^-\to Zh$ and the Higgs diphoton decay channel. Our findings indicate that the Higgs diphoton process offers superior sensitivity compared to the $Zh$ production channel. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the model can be effectively constrained by current experimental data.

This paper addresses operators on a complex Hilbert space, focusing specifically on the characterization of the subdifferential for the sum of two operators' numerical radii. First, we provide a formula for the generalized Legendre-Fenchel transform applied to squared numerical radius functions. Subsequently, we demonstrate that for any pair of bounded operators $A$ and $B$ on Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, the first-order Fréchet subdifferential of $f(T) = \frac{1}{2}(\text{w}(AT)^2 + \text{w}(BT)^2)$ at $T$ comprises all operators $S$ satisfying the condition $\langle (AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* + AT^*S B^* +

Differential privacy (DP) is a rigorous mathematical framework designed to safeguard individual privacy within datasets. Although DP has been extensively researched and applied in various domains, its utility in the finance sector remains underexplored. This paper introduces a comprehensive survey of DP applications specifically for finance, covering areas such as data publishing, machine learning, and statistical analysis. We begin by outlining the foundational concepts of DP, followed by a detailed examination of DP-enhanced financial services. Furthermore, we identify critical unresolved challenges and outline potential future research trajectories.

This study examines the correlation structure of a stochastic mapping $X$ defined on a graph $G$ with $n$ nodes, where the mapping assigns each node to a distinct target. We establish that the correlation between the mappings of any two nodes is governed by the length of the shortest path connecting them. Additionally, we introduce a novel model for generating random dispersion fields on graphs, which serves as a specific instance of the stochastic mapping framework. We demonstrate that, under certain conditions, the correlation structure of this mapping can be approximated using a Poisson process.

This study examines the initiation of high-pressure (up to 100 bar) explosive gas mixtures of He-H2-O2 using a laser source. The laser, which is unfocused and has a relatively low power, is applied to a solid target to generate a plasma that serves as the ignition source. The research investigates how varying the laser's position relative to the mixture influences the resulting reaction volume. Additionally, the impact of helium concentration on the reaction volume is analyzed. The findings indicate that the reaction volume is highly sensitive to the distance between the laser-induced plasma and the combustible gas. Furthermore, increasing helium concentration significantly reduces the maximum reaction volume, a trend that correlates with a decrease in the mixture's sensitivity.

This study introduces a new method for semantic segmentation designed to enhance boundary awareness. The approach employs a dual-branch architecture: a primary branch processes the entire image to generate the final segmentation map, while a secondary branch analyzes image boundaries to produce a dedicated boundary map. This boundary map is subsequently integrated into the primary branch to refine the segmentation output. The network architecture is designed to be lightweight, making it well-suited for deployment on mobile devices and web platforms. Experimental results demonstrate that this method achieves state-of-the-art performance on the PASCAL-Context dataset and delivers strong results on the MS-COCO dataset.

This paper introduces a driver messenger system designed to facilitate communication between vehicle occupants, specifically targeting a lane-change assistance scenario. The objective is to enhance safety during lane transitions by allowing a driver to detect blind spots and receive confirmation from a passenger before maneuvering. The study outlines the system's architecture, implementation, and validation. The proposed system is built upon a collaborative infrastructure that integrates a 5G network with edge computing, utilizing a Raspberry Pi for data processing and a 3D-printed vehicle model as a physical prototype. The system's functionality is verified through a series of experiments.

This study examines the impact of boundaries on noninteracting weakly active particles within diverse geometric configurations. Utilizing the Smoluchowski framework, we analyze the steady-state distribution of these particles across spherical, cylindrical, and planar geometries. We demonstrate that the system's symmetry dictates the distribution of particle orientations. Furthermore, we investigate the temporal evolution of the system, specifically the mean orientation and polarization, alongside the mean-squared displacement and the first-passage time. Our findings indicate that the first-passage time is governed by the active force magnitude, domain size, and the specific geometry of the system.

The average particle model with a single-particle basis is extended to incorporate Siegert states, which are quasinormal modes characterized by outgoing boundary conditions. This modification enables the systematic calculation of electromagnetic transition matrix elements and provides a more realistic depiction of time-reversal symmetry breaking within the nuclear mean field. We demonstrate that these electromagnetic properties are computed using a straightforward, closed-form expression. Furthermore, we outline a new methodology for deriving electromagnetic form factors and present an initial application of this approach to the $^{12}$C nucleus.

This study presents an analysis of the 2018-07-13 X-class flare using the Solar Dynamics Observatory's Imaging Telescope (SDO/AIA) and the Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS). By examining the 155.7 Å band, which captures Si IV emission, we identified a rapid, 0.1-second cadence variation in the flare's early phase. These spectral fluctuations occur on a timescale of approximately 0.2 seconds, with a peak intensity lasting about 0.5 seconds. The flare's onset is marked by a sudden rise in the continuum, accompanied by a sharp increase in the Si IV line's equivalent width. The continuum intensity rises by a factor of 1.5, while the equivalent width increases by 1.2 times. The spectral line's full width at half maximum (FWHM) expands by 1.2 times, and the peak intensity grows by 1.5 times. The strong CP problem is resolved by introducing the axion, which serves as the Nambu-Goldstone boson arising from the spontaneous breaking of the Peccei-Quinn symmetry; consequently, it is predicted to exhibit a small electric dipole moment. The current experimental upper limits on this value are stringent, yet the theoretical mass and coupling constants of the axion remain largely unknown. This paper investigates the axion's potential nature, specifically addressing its status as a composite particle, by analyzing the dynamics of the PQ sector. We demonstrate that the axion's properties are contingent upon the specific ultraviolet completion of the theory.

This study examines the impact of collision cascade dynamics on the nanopatterning of thin, irradiated materials. We demonstrate that the critical angle for nanopatterning is governed by the ratio of the projected ion energy to the specific energy required to generate a surface feature. Furthermore, we show that the ion energy projection is dictated by the kinematics of the first primary nuclear collision, whereas the specific energy deposition relies on the characteristics of the collision cascade. Ultimately, we establish that the critical angle is controlled by the balance between the first primary collision's kinematics and the attributes of the first primary collision's target atom.

Plagiarism detection in source code is a complex issue that has garnered significant attention from both academic and industrial sectors. While numerous existing tools and approaches aim to identify plagiarism, they often fail to provide a comprehensive solution. This paper introduces a novel anti-plagiarism methodology based on "pathways," which are defined as ordered sequences of keywords extracted from source code. We present a proof-of-concept implementation written in C# that demonstrates the practical application of this approach.

This paper investigates the complete convergence of Dirichlet series within automorphic forms, specifically defined as $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{a_n}{s^n}$ for $s \in \mathbb{C}$. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the complete convergence of these series, which are expressed in terms of the corresponding complete, bounded mean value conditions.

This work examines near subgroups within the context of metric groups. We establish that any group possessing a near subgroup is quasi-isometric to an OS-simply-connected group that has a near subgroup. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the quasi-isometry class of an infinite OS-stable compact group is entirely determined by its near subgroups.

This study introduces a novel computational framework for estimating log-concave densities. The method employs a new, nonparametric Bayesian estimator that utilizes a mixture of truncated normal distributions, which is derived through a re-parameterization of the convex support. This approach offers greater computational efficiency compared to existing methods. Additionally, the paper demonstrates the estimator's consistency and validates its performance through both simulation experiments and an application to real data.

This study introduces a computational approach for sampling granular microstates within a canonical volume ensemble. By employing the Wang-Landau algorithm, we determine the density of states for a two-dimensional system of frictional disks subject to isotropic repulsion and a uniform gravitational field. This method is grounded in the principle that the system's entropy is a function of its volume. We demonstrate that the Wang-Landau technique effectively yields the system's entropy across various volumes, enabling the calculation of the system's equation of state.

This study examines a two-player game played on a graph, where one player, the director, seeks to guide the other, the adventurer, to a designated target vertex. The director possesses a limited set of available moves that are applied globally to the graph structure, whereas the adventurer controls a local path, choosing a neighbor for the director's node at each turn. The director's primary objective is to formulate a sequence of moves that guarantees the meeting of the two players, regardless of the adventurer's choices. We demonstrate that the director can achieve this goal if and only if the graph is connected and has a maximum degree of 2.

We introduce a novel method for analyzing Gaussian processes, defined by the assumption that the squared frequency of the most probable single-trajectory event scales linearly with the square of the frequency of the process's stationary two-time autocorrelation function. This relationship is established through a rigorous derivation of spectral densities for both scenarios, utilizing single-trajectory and two-time Fourier transforms. This framework is applied to investigate the spectral characteristics of a two-dimensional Brownian particle subject to an external potential.

This study investigates the (1+1)-dimensional higher-order Broer-Kaup system utilizing the high-order conserved quantities and the reciprocal nonlinear method. By deriving a corresponding high-order system through the application of these methods, we analyze the interaction behavior between solitons and polynomials. Specifically, we identify that the interaction involves soliton-soliton four-layers, along with interactions between a single layer of either a soliton or polynomials.

This work investigates the weak solutions to the incompressible Euler equations for an ideal fluid within a bounded three-dimensional domain. By utilizing a Biot-Savart type representation for the velocity field, we establish a general criterion ensuring the conservation of kinetic energy. Furthermore, we demonstrate that under specific conditions, these constructed weak solutions exhibit smooth behavior.

The Virtual Reality Universe Project (VIRUP) is a collaborative initiative designed to create an immersive virtual reality experience of the cosmos, allowing users to freely explore the Universe. This project is being developed by the University of the Basque Country (UPV/EHU) in collaboration with the University of the Algarve (UA). The initiative aims to provide a comprehensive and accessible educational tool for the public, offering a unique opportunity to virtually traverse the Universe. The project's primary objective is to deliver an interactive, educational, and entertaining experience of the Universe.
